stem.en: A ball moves on a smooth surface with no friction. A net force now acts on it, opposite to its direction of motion. What happens to its speed?

feedback.en: Right. The net force acts against the motion, so the ball slows down.
The speed stays the same only when the net force is zero. Here a net force acts.
The speed increases when the net force acts along the motion. Here it acts opposite to the motion.

explanation.en: A net force changes the velocity in its own direction. A net force opposite to the motion makes the ball slow down.

hints.en: Does the net force act along the motion or against it?
